svg.title: Three AI risk frameworks and the question each one answers
svg.desc: Three panels. NIST AI RMF 1.0 supplies voluntary governance structure through the Govern, Map, Measure, and Manage functions. The OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications supplies a ranked application risk list, shown here as the 2025 edition with its ten identifiers. MITRE ATLAS supplies observed adversary tactics against AI systems. A footer notes that the three answer different questions and that the OWASP list was re-ranked in an August 2026 edition.
svg.text: Three AI risk frameworks, three different questions
Governance structure, ranked application risk, and observed adversary behavior. None of the three substitutes for another.
NIST AI RMF 1.0 — VOLUNTARY, JANUARY 2023
“How do we decide and govern?”
GOVERN — culture, policy, risk tolerance, accountability
MAP — context, dependencies, and system scoping
MEASURE — empirical testing and adversarial evaluation
MANAGE — risk response, controls, and AI incident handling
OWASP TOP 10 FOR LLM APPLICATIONS — 2025 EDITION
“What goes wrong in these applications?”
LLM01 Prompt Injection · LLM02 Sensitive Information Disclosure
LLM03 Supply Chain · LLM04 Data and Model Poisoning
LLM05 Improper Output Handling · LLM06 Excessive Agency
LLM07–LLM10 System Prompt Leakage, Vector and Embedding
Weaknesses, Misinformation, Unbounded Consumption
MITRE ATLAS — ADVERSARIAL THREAT LANDSCAPE FOR ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS
“What has actually been done to systems like this?”
Reconnaissance → Initial Access (poisoned data, backdoored weights, indirect injection) → Execution (unsafe deserialization,
unintended tool calls) → Exfiltration (hidden context, memorized records, model weights) → Impact (evasion, exhaustion, unauthorized action)
A knowledge base of observed behavior — not a control catalog.
Use them together: ATLAS and OWASP tell you what to look for; the AI RMF tells you how to decide what to do about it.
The OWASP list is versioned — a 2026 edition published in August 2026 re-ranked several entries, so always cite the edition you mean.
